svg.title: Hoang Khanh · Multi-tier silicon solar system
svg.desc: Exaggerated exposed semiconductor package with a patterned silicon die, gold bond wires, layered green substrate and silver BGA balls, four vendors, ten MCU and SoC models locked to a rigid rotating ring, and fourteen counter-rotating technology capsules. Layer-two chip centers stay 36 degrees apart and rotate at the same constant 3.75 degrees per second, completing a lap in 96 seconds. Circular-plane rotation starts from a 520 by 210 ellipse. A shared 32-second forward pitch gradually settles the core and all three rings; perspective expands the foreground and recedes the rear. Counter-rotation keeps MCU labels and vendor stations facing the camera. Functional cards on the outer ring follow the same plane pitch as the core and rings, including perspective compression. The die retains its vertical thickness as its top plane tilts. No independent chip drift or overtaking occurs. Brand logos rise and sink atop translucent energy volumes shaped to their original outlines, including inner cutouts, connected from the package underside through matching openings in the lid. Their shaded contour walls, boundary light columns and logo-shaped caps extend continuously with the logo, glowing in their vendor colors on a 4.8-second energy cycle. Local satellites retain separate motion. QFN side contacts, LQFP gull-wing leads and underside LGA lands replace generic pins. The outer belt represents ecosystem capabilities rather than features of every chip. A static composition is provided for reduced motion.
